description: Reverend Samuel Green was a free Black Methodist preacher and Underground Railroad agent in Dorchester County, Maryland who had purchased his own freedom in 1833. In spring 1857, after the escape of the "Dover Eight," he was arrested and tried when police found a map of Canada, a letter from his escaped slave son and railroad schedules in his home. He was acquitted then immediately tried again, this time for possessing a copy of Uncle Tom's Cabin in violation of a Maryland law against abolitionist literature. He was convicted in May 1857 and sentenced to ten years in the state penitentiary. Governor Augustus W. Bradford granted him a conditional pardon on March 26, 1862, on the conditions he would leave the state within sixty days. He was released on April 21, 1862, having served nearly five years.
